tools.name: execute_compute_task
tools.title: Executes a compute task
tools.description:
Executes a python function on the created compute environment. 
    Depending on the complexity of the code and the input/output data sizes this can either resolve in minutes to hours.
    This tool will move the compute task to processing, but the task can still end up with an error as resullt if the code crashes or if the output is invalid.

taskId.description: The id of the task on which to execute the python function

file.description:
String with the python function to execute. This python function named "userFunction" should have 1 input parameter 
      which will be dict. The raster layers from the create task step can be accessed in the input parameter with their timestampId as 
      key and will be a dict with properties raster (numpy array with raster image values of dimensions number of bands * 256 pixels 
      * 256 pixels, the last band is always an alpha band), transform (a rasterio transform object) and extent (a dict with 
      properties xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax). The vector layers from create task can be accessed in the input parameter with their 
      timestampId as key and will be a dict with property vector being a geopandas geodataframe. The files from create task can be
      found under their path id as key and will be available as an io BytesIO. 
      Output must be possible to json.dump for largeResponse = False and must be an io BytesIO otherwise, illegal outputs will error the task.

writeToLayer.description: Specifies the destination layer to write the file result to.

tools.description: Creates a compute task environment with the given specification. It usually takes up to a few minutes for the requested environment to be prepared.

interpreter.description: The interpreter of the task, for example python3.12. Currently only python is supported.

requirements.description: The python packages required for the task, should be formatted like a requirements.txt so it can be pip installed.

nodes.description: The number of nodes to prepare to run the task, the compute load is spread out over these nodes.

layers.description: Array of json objects with properties pathId and timestampId describing the map data layers that will be available during the task.

files.description: Array with the path ids of the paths of type file to use during the compute.

largeResult.description: Boolean whether the result of the task is going to be a file or a json.
